title: Morse Critical Points Hessians and Indices

items.title: Critical points and critical values of a smooth function
The intrinsic Hessian of a smooth function at a critical point
Critical-point Hessian matrices transform by congruence under chart changes
items.strategy: Write the second derivatives after a chart change. At a critical point the first-derivative correction terms vanish, leaving the Jacobian-transpose congruence relation between the two Hessian matrices.

items.title: Riemannian metrics, symmetric cotangent-bundle connections, and covariant Hessians
A Riemannian metric has a unique Levi-Civita connection on the cotangent bundle
items.strategy: In a local orthonormal coframe, solve the structure equations for a unique skew-symmetric matrix of one-forms. The induced cotangent-bundle connection is symmetric and metric-compatible, and uniqueness lets the local constructions glue globally.

items.title: At a critical point, the intrinsic Hessian agrees with the Levi-Civita Hessian
items.strategy: In local coordinates the Levi-Civita covariant Hessian equals second derivatives minus Christoffel-symbol terms multiplied by first derivatives. At a critical point those first-derivative terms vanish, so the Levi-Civita and intrinsic critical Hessians coincide.

items.title: Nondegenerate critical points, nullity, index, and coindex
Sylvester inertia makes the Morse index intrinsic
items.strategy: Item 3 shows all chart Hessian matrices are congruent. Sylvester's law fixes the positive, negative, and zero counts of a real symmetric form under congruence, so index, coindex, and nullity are chart-independent.

items.title: Morse functions and excellent Morse functions
Nondegenerate critical points are isolated
items.strategy: In a local chart, the coefficients of df form the gradient map of the coordinate representative. Its derivative at the critical point is the Hessian matrix, so nondegeneracy gives an invertible derivative; the inverse function theorem then makes the zero of df isolated.

items.title: A Morse function on a compact manifold has finitely many critical points
items.strategy: Each critical point has an open neighbourhood containing no other critical point, and each noncritical point has an open neighbourhood containing none. These sets cover the compact manifold, so a finite subcover uses only finitely many critical-point neighbourhoods.

items.title: A nonzero second derivative splits off a signed square with a smooth parameter
items.strategy: Factor a one-variable germ with nonzero second derivative as a signed square times a positive smooth unit, then absorb the unit by a smooth coordinate change.

items.title: Splitting one Morse coordinate preserves the residual Hessian
items.strategy: After one coordinate change splits off a signed square, differentiate the transformed expression twice at the critical point. The remaining quadratic part is the restriction of the original Hessian to the unsplit coordinates.

items.title: Morse lemma
items.strategy: Diagonalize the critical Hessian by a linear change of coordinates, split off one signed square with item 12, track the residual nondegenerate Hessian with item 13, and finish by induction on the dimension, keeping the endpoint cases explicit.

items.title: The Morse index detects local extrema and saddles
items.strategy: Read the sign of the Morse normal form. No negative squares gives a strict local minimum, all negative squares gives a strict local maximum, and mixed signs give nearby points on both sides of the critical value.

items.title: Index and coindex swap under negation
items.strategy: Negating the Hessian swaps positive and negative directions and leaves the kernel unchanged.

items.title: The critical level is a quadratic cone in Morse coordinates
items.strategy: Set the Morse normal form equal to the critical value. The critical level becomes |x^-|^2 = |x^+|^2, with the index-0 and index-n cases collapsing to the single critical point.

items.title: The zero-dimensional Morse convention

title: Morse Critical Points Hessians and Indices — Examples

items.title: The height function on the sphere is a perfect Morse function
items.strategy: For h(x)=x_{n+1} on S^n, solve dh=0 by tangent-space orthogonality and compute the local quadratic form in pole charts. The north and south poles give the unique index-n and index-0 critical points.

items.title: The standard quadratic form realizes every Morse index
items.strategy: The diagonal quadratic form already is in Morse normal form, so its unique critical point at the origin has the prescribed index by inspection of the Hessian.

items.title: A standard torus height function has four critical points
items.strategy: For f(x,y)=cos(2πx)+cos(2πy) on T^2, solve the sine equations to locate the four critical points and read each index from the diagonal Hessian.

items.title: An isolated critical point can be degenerate
items.strategy: For f(x)=x^4, the derivative vanishes only at 0, but the second derivative at 0 is zero, so the critical point is isolated and degenerate.

items.title: A degenerate critical set can be nonisolated
items.strategy: For f(x,y)=x^2, the differential is (2x,0), so every point with x=0 is critical, producing a degenerate nonisolated critical line.

items.title: The empty and zero-dimensional Morse cases
items.strategy: On the empty manifold there are no points to check. On a finite discrete 0-manifold, every tangent space is zero and every point is therefore a nondegenerate index-0 critical point for any smooth real-valued function.
